title: Shadow-run billing validator for canary attribution rules
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a shadow/parallel execution path for the billing attribution pipeline so new attribution rules, sampling heuristics, and grouping logic can be validated against production results without affecting invoices. The goal is to run the new logic in 'read-only' mode for a configurable subset of traffic (by tenant or sampling fraction), capture per-request deltas (tokens, route mapping, model variant costs), compute summary drift metrics, and surface mismatches in a Grafana dashboard and nightly report. This will let PM/Finance/Platform teams iterate on attribution changes and roll them out with quantitative guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: Shadow validator can be toggled per-cluster and per-tenant via a feature flag; default off
For a 5% sample across N tenants, the shadow pipeline runs and writes comparison rows to a separate namespace without touching production billing sinks
Daily drift report produced showing top 20 tenants by absolute cost delta and distribution of per-request token differences
Alerting rule created if median per-tenant cost delta > 4% for more than 6 hours
End-to-end latency of shadow run does not increase critical path latencies; shadow run resources are isolated and bounded
Runbook updated with steps to disable shadow-run, inspect diffs, and promote rule changes to gating rollout
steps: Design data schema for comparison rows: original_tokens, shadow_tokens, original_route, shadow_route, model_variant_diff, timestamp, tenant_id, request_id
Implement a lightweight proxy in the metering gateway to fork a copy of normalized events to shadow Kafka topic
Build a stateless consumer (shadow-validator) that applies the new attribution rules and writes diffs to a compact Parquet store on s3://redwood-shadow-billing/YYYY/MM/DD/
Create daily batch job to aggregate diffs into tenant-level metrics and push to metrics DB for Grafana
Add feature-flag controls and per-tenant sampling config in Console; expose UI toggle for SEs to enable shadow runs for customer demos
Instrument cost guardrails and create Grafana dashboard and Alertmanager rule
updates: 2026-02-12 - Ava Chen: Kickoff meeting with PM (Sofia Ramirez) and Finance (Liam O'Neal). Consensus: start with sampling-based approach rather than full traffic mirror to limit S3/costs.

2026-02-18 - Marcus Patel: Spike complete for Kafka fork in metering gateway. Proof-of-concept forwards normalized consumption events to shadow topic; small perf impact (~0.6ms p95). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/412

2026-02-25 - Marcus Patel: Schema drafted and reviewed with Data Eng. Chosen schema minimizes wide rows and uses codes for route/model to reduce storage. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Shadow+Billing+Validator+Design

2026-03-03 - Data Eng (review): Recommended compact Parquet with daily partitioning and 7-day retention for initial run. Trade-off: shorter retention lowers cost but reduces historical debugging window.
2026-03-07 - Marcus Patel: Implemented shadow-validator consumer and end-to-end pipeline in staging. Artifacts: github.com/redwood-inference/analytics/tree/feat/shadow-validator
2026-03-09 - QA (Priya Shah): Ran 48h shadow against synthetic traffic for five tenants. Found 0.9% median token discrepancy due to an edge-case in prefix caching logic; created follow-up ENG-47232.

2026-03-12 - Marcus Patel: Dashboard prototype live (Grafana). Alerting thresholds pending finance sign-off. PR opened to add feature-flag and sampling UI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/578
notes: Primary risk is storage/compute cost — mitigation: strict sampling, 7-day default retention, and monitor S3 usage per-customer. Secondary risk: subtle logic mismatches (prefix cache, batching boundaries). We will gate rollouts behind drift alerts and finance approval.
stakeholder_notes: Finance wants a CSV export capability for the nightly report. Sales/SEs want per-tenant enablement for customer demos. Keep UX simple: enable -> collects diffs but does not affect billing.
